Question_text: A student electrolyses three solutions using the apparatus shown. Complete the table. Give a test and observation to identify oxygen gas.

Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(I). A student investigates the rate of this reaction at three different temperatures using the apparatus shown. What is meant by an excess of calcium carbonate? Name the two pieces of apparatus, A and B. The student does experiment 1 at 20 °C. Name a piece of apparatus that can be used to keep the temperature constant. The student does two more experiments: experiment 2 at 40 °C, experiment 3 at 60 °C. Suggest two variables that the student keeps constant so that temperature is the only variable that affects the rate of reaction. The student plots a graph of the results. Describe how the graphs are used to decide which experiment has the fastest rate. Write a number in each box on the graph to identify experiments 1, 2 and 3. State how the graph shows that the reactions stop. Why do the reactions stop?

Carbon and copper(II) oxide are both black solids. Copper(II) oxide reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to form an aqueous solution. Carbon does not react with or dissolve in dilute sulfuric acid. Neither carbon nor copper(II) oxide dissolve in water. A mixture contains carbon and copper(II) oxide only. Plan an experiment to produce a sample of pure carbon from the mixture.

A student is provided with three solutions: aqueous zinc sulfate, aqueous copper(II) sulfate, aqueous calcium nitrate. The student tests the three aqueous solutions by adding each reagent shown in the table. Record the observations in the table. Write 'no reaction' where appropriate.
Unit: UNIT 12: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis

Question_text: Solution J is bleach. A student does an experiment to determine the concentration of sodium chlorate(I), NaClO, in J. The student transfers 25.0cm³ of J to a conical flask using a pipette. Why does the student use a pipette instead of a measuring cylinder to measure 25.0cm³ of J? Which other piece of apparatus could be used to measure 25.0cm³ of J? The student adds an excess of aqueous sodium iodide and an excess of hydrochloric acid to the conical flask. A reaction occurs to form iodine. This is solution K. The amount of iodine produced can be determined by titration with aqueous sodium thiosulfate, Na2S2O3, with a suitable indicator. Solution L is 0.0500 mol/dm³ Na2S2O3. L is put into a burette and run into the conical flask until the end-point is reached. Why is it wrong to wash out the burette with water immediately before filling it with L? Three titrations are done. The diagrams show parts of the burette with the liquid levels at the beginning and end of each titration. Use the diagrams to complete the table. Tick (✔) the best titration results in the table. Use these best results to calculate the average volume of L. Calculate the number of moles of Na2S2O3 in the average volume of L, 0.0500mol/dm³ Na2S2O3, used in the titration. Use the equation to calculate the number of moles of I₂ in 25.0cm³ of K. 2Na2S2O3 + I2 Na2S4O6 + 2NaI Use the equation to calculate the number of moles of NaClO that produces the number of moles of I2 calculated in (f). NaClO + 2NaI + 2HCl I2 + 3NaCl + H2O. Calculate the M₁ of NaClO. [A₁: Na, 23; Cl, 35.5; O, 16] Use your answers to (g) and (h) to calculate the mass of NaClO in 25.0cm³ of J. Calculate the concentration of NaClO in J: in g/dm³, in mol/dm³.
Topic: 3.3 The mole and the Avogadro constant

Question_text: When zinc is added to aqueous iron(II) sulfate, the temperature of the mixture increases. The equation for the reaction is shown. Zn(s) + FeSO4(aq) ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s). A student transfers 25.0cm³ of 2.0mol/dm³ iron(II) sulfate into a beaker. The temperature of this solution is 22.0°C. The student then adds excess zinc to the aqueous iron(II) sulfate and starts a timer. The student stirs the mixture with a thermometer and measures the temperature at 1 minute intervals. The results are shown. As soon as the zinc is added to the aqueous iron(II) sulfate, the temperature of the mixture increases. What can you deduce about the reaction from this information? Why do the temperature readings in the table decrease from 1.0 to 6.0 minutes? If the student had continued to measure the temperatures after 6.0 minutes, suggest the lowest temperature that would be reached. Plot the results from the table on the grid. Draw a straight line of best-fit. Extend the line until it intersects with the y-axis. On the grid, draw a circle around the anomalous point. Use your graph to determine the temperature of the mixture at a time of 2.5 minutes. Use your graph to determine the time at which the temperature of the mixture would be 30.0°C. Use your graph to determine the temperature of the mixture at 0.0 minutes. This figure represents the maximum temperature that the mixture reaches in the reaction. The initial temperature of the aqueous iron(II) sulfate was 22.0°C. Calculate the maximum temperature rise after the zinc is added. The student uses 25.0 cm³ of 2.0mol/dm³ iron(II) sulfate and an excess of zinc. Calculate the number of moles of iron(II) sulfate in 25.0cm³ of 2.0mol/dm³ iron(II) sulfate. The heat produced in the reaction in kJ/mol is calculated using the expression shown.
